extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners and patent applicants/agents (KIPO procedures)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for examining Korean patent applications, covering priority claims (international and domestic), disclosure exceptions, divisional/converted applications, legitimate-right-holder filings, and national-phase PCT specifics. Focused on claim-by-claim reference-date determination, evidentiary and timing requirements, examiner actions, and scope/retroactivity rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim validity despite later fate of first application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed in the first country that is invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned or rejected after filing can still serve as a basis for claiming a right of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner shall not examine whether the first-country application which forms the basis of the priority claim is pending. The subsequent fate of the first application (invalidated/withdrawn/etc.) does not by itself prevent its use as a priority basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date determined on a claim-by-claim basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date for determining patentability is determined in principle on a claim-by-claim basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must evaluate each claimed invention separately when deciding which filing/priority date is the relevant reference date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date for inventions identical to first-country application
rubrics_metrics.description: For an invention identical (including substantially/de facto identical) to the invention of the application filed in the first country, the reference date shall be the filing date of the application in the first country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple priority claims are involved, the reference date for an invention commonly described in two or more first-country applications is the earliest filing date among those applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date for inventions not described in first-country application
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions not described in an application filed in the first country, the filing date of the application claiming priority under the treaty shall be the reference date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claimed invention is obtained by combining technical matters separately included in two or more first-country applications, or combining those and a new technical matter, it is treated as not described in the first-country applications (i.e., reference date is the filing date of the later application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority not recognized when first-country application itself claims earlier priority
rubrics_metrics.description: When the first-country application (that would serve as the basis) claims priority based on another earlier application, that first-country application shall not be regarded as the 'earliest application' for the invention described in both applications; the effect of the priority claim shall not be recognized for that invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination in this case shall not be retroactively conducted to the reference date and the examiner shall notify a specific reason for non-retroactive application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must specify reason for non-retroactive application when prior art prevents retroactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: If, during search, the examiner discovers prior art such that retroactive application of the reference date is not possible, the examiner shall specify the reason for non-retroactive application in the notice of grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specific explanation must be included in communications to the applicant (e.g., notice of grounds for rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidential documents for priority: submission deadline and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidential documents for a priority claim must be submitted within one year and four months from the earliest filing date; failure to submit within this statutory period causes the priority claim to lose its effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will request a procedural amendment if evidential documents are missing and will invalidate the priority claim procedure if the deficiency is not amended. Submission after the statutory period cannot cure the procedural deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAS / online-exchange exemption for submission of description/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the description or drawings of the first-country application can be exempted from submission if applications are filed in countries equipped with an online system for exchange of evidential documents (DAS) and those agencies agree to online delivery (e.g., Japan, EPO, US, WIPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where DAS/on-line delivery is available and used, examiners accept electronic access in lieu of paper copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application-number indication may substitute for evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicating the application number of the first-country application in the application claiming priority may substitute for submission of documents stating that application number in accordance with Article 54(4)(ii) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where properly indicated, the application number can be relied upon instead of submitting full evidentiary copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations of evidential documents may be required
rubrics_metrics.description: If considered necessary (e.g., due to prior art in the period between the priority date and the later filing), the examiner may set a time period and request submission of translations (into Korean) of the evidential documents for the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required translations in Korean within the prescribed period may lead to invalidation of the priority claim procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority: eligible claimant
rubrics_metrics.description: A person eligible to claim domestic priority is an applicant of the prior-filed application. If the applicant of the prior-filed and later-filed applications are not the same, the examiner shall request amendments and invalidate the priority claim procedure if the deficiency is not cured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of amendment requests is limited to correction of obvious errors. The determination whether applicants are the same is made as of the time the domestic priority claim is filed (cover sheet or subsequent amendment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority: one-year time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The domestic priority claim must be made within one year from the filing date of the prior-filed application which forms the basis of the domestic priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed after the statutory period the examiner requests amendments and invalidates the priority claim procedure if the deficiency is not cured; scope of allowed amendments limited to obvious errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional/converted applications cannot be basis of domestic priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional or converted applications shall not serve as a basis of a domestic priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the domestic priority claim is based on a divisional/converted application, the examiner requests amendments and invalidates the priority claim procedure if not cured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application finality bars domestic priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the prior-filed application has been invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or where decisions to grant/reject have become conclusive and binding, that application cannot serve as a basis of a domestic priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner requests amendments and invalidates the priority claim procedure if the deficiency is not cured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date rules for domestic priority (identical / not stated / combinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For domestic priority claims the reference date is determined claim-by-claim: (i) identical inventions: reference date = filing date of the prior-filed application (earliest if multiple); (ii) inventions not stated in the prior-filed original specification: reference date = filing date of the domestic priority claim; (iii) combinations of matters from two or more prior-filed applications (or combining new matter) are treated as inventions not stated in the original specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior-filed application itself claims priority to another application, the effect of the domestic priority claim is not recognized for inventions stated in both; examiner to specify reasons for non-retroactive application where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions when prior-filed application causes conflicts (domestic priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner discovers that the application under examination has become a basis for a domestic priority claim, he/she shall defer further examination. If the domestic priority claim is invalidated due to formalities, the examiner shall resume examination promptly and consider the application withdrawn/suspended as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision to grant a patent on the domestic priority claim shall be deferred until the prior-filed application is considered withdrawn. For expedited examination, the examiner shall notify the applicant that grant will be deferred until withdrawal of the prior-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure exceptions: statutory filing window
rubrics_metrics.description: An application claiming disclosure exceptions under Article 30(2) must be filed within twelve months (six months for applications filed before March 14, 2012) from the prescribed publication date indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed after the statutory period the examiner requests amendments and invalidates the claim if the deficiency is not cured. An untimely claim is considered not overcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure exception based on publication by entitled person: evidentiary checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Where disclosure exception is claimed because publication was made by a person entitled to obtain a patent, the examiner shall examine whether the discloser is entitled, whether the claim is made in the application, and whether evidential documents of the public disclosure were submitted within thirty days from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deficiencies are discovered the examiner requests amendments and invalidates the claim if not cured within the prescribed period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure-exception special-attention cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must pay special attention where: (a) the person who made the public disclosure and the applicant are not the same; (b) the type and date of public disclosure are stated incorrectly; (c) submitted evidential documents are not sufficient to specify the invention in the public disclosure; (d) evidential documents are submitted without stating the purport of the disclosure-exception claim in the application (only when evidential docs are submitted on the filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are typical anti-patterns that may cause invalidation of a disclosure-exception claim if not corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple public disclosures and evidentiary submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiple public disclosures, if the purport of disclosure exceptions is indicated in the application and evidential documents for each disclosure are submitted, exceptions shall be applied to each disclosure. Where disclosures have an inseparable relation, submission of evidential documents for the initial disclosure may suffice for subsequent ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an exhibition display and subsequent market sale ordinarily require separate evidential documents unless the sales are closely connected to the exhibition (e.g., by contract), in which case exemption may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy judged claim-by-claim for multiple disclosure-exception claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiple claims of disclosure exceptions, the legitimacy of each claim shall be judged separately for each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a disclosure-exception claim is recognized as legitimate, novelty and inventive step are judged as if the concerned invention had not been publicly known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a divisional/converted application
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional or converted application may only be filed by an applicant of the original application. If applicants differ, the examiner shall provide an opportunity for petition and then return the application to an applicant; amendments to correct applicants are limited to obvious errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision whether applicants are the same is made as of the time the divisional/converted application is submitted; changes to applicant name on the divisional filing date are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing windows for filing division or conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional must be filed only during the period designated for amendment of specification/drawings or within three months from service of a certified copy of the decision to grant (or certain trial decisions) (but not after patent registration), or during the appeal period against a decision to reject. A converted application must be filed within thirty days from receiving a certified copy of the decision to reject (or extended period if approved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an appeal is requested, a divisional may be filed within thirty days from transmittal of the certified copy of the decision to reject (or extended period under Article 132(3)). If filed after the statutory period the examiner provides opportunity for petition and then returns the application pursuant to enforcement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division/conversion barred if original terminated or final
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an original application has been invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or where a decision to reject is conclusive and binding, division or conversion shall not be made based on that original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the original application falls under these cases the examiner shall provide an opportunity for petition and then return the application. If division/conversion was filed legitimately before termination, the divisional is still regarded as valid and examination begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope-of-disclosure requirement for division/converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters described in the specification or drawings of divisional applications must be within the scope of matters described in the original specification/drawings of the parent application; division/conversion out of that scope is treated differently depending on the original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For originals filed before Sep 30, 2006: examiner delivers preliminary notice for inadmissible division/conversion; if not cured, deliver notice for inadmissible division and conduct examination as of the divisional filing date (not retroactive) unless scope violation legitimately cured during examination—then retroactive. For originals filed after Oct 1, 2006: deliver written notice of ground for rejection by reason of scope violation and, if not cured, make a decision to reject. Where both scope violation and other grounds for rejection exist, admissibility of division/conversion is normally confirmed before notifying other grounds, but simultaneous notices may be given if unrelated to retroactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-division identity and Article 36(2) consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a divisional application is made legally and a claimed invention of the divisional is identical to a claimed invention of the original application after the division, the applications shall be subject to Article 36(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to the original application are required and must be made as of the filing date of the divisional application (Enforcement Rules Article 29(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-level division validity
rubrics_metrics.description: If an original application A is divided into B and B is further divided into C, then C is legitimate and deemed filed at the filing date of A provided that B meets division requirements relative to A and C meets division requirements relative to B, and the invention of C is within the scope of the original disclosure of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converted applications are treated in the same manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by a legitimate right holder: four requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be recognized as an application by a legitimate right holder (Articles 34 and 35), the following must be met: (1) an application by an unentitled person was filed earlier than the legitimate holder's application; (2) the unentitled person's application is rejected or invalidated in trial on the ground it was not filed by the entitled person; (3) the legitimate holder's application is filed within thirty days from when the trial decision became conclusive and unappealable; and (4) the scope of the claimed invention in the legitimate holder's application falls within the disclosure of the unentitled person's application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filed with Form (xiv) or legitimacy argued in written argument during examination, the examiner shall study legitimacy before any other grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions when legitimacy is in doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner doubts the applicant's legitimacy regarding requirements (1), (3) or (4), he/she shall deliver a notice stating that the filing date shall not be retroactive. If requirement (2) is not satisfied, except for special cases, examination shall be deferred until a decision becomes final and conclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination is resumed promptly after the decision on patentability or invalidation trial is final and conclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of recognition as legitimate right holder
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application is recognized as an application by the legitimate right holder, it is deemed to have been filed on the date when the unentitled person's application was filed; judgments of patent requirements, period calculations, and related provisions are determined as of that earlier date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects the legitimate holder against intervening third-party applications filed after the unentitled person's earlier filing but before the legitimate-holder filing (example explained).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate-right-holder scope limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of invention in an application by the legitimate holder is limited to the claimed inventions and those disclosed in the specification or drawings of the unentitled person's application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the legitimate holder's application includes inventions beyond that disclosure (e.g., multiple inventions where only some fall within the disclosed scope), the filing date for those beyond-scope inventions shall not be retroactive in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: International patent application treated as regular application with PCT-specific exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An international patent application under the PCT where Korea is a designated State is treated as a regular patent application filed on the international filing date, except for certain exceptions including an enlarged concept of novelty. A foreign-language international application is deemed withdrawn if its Korean translation is not submitted according to Article 201.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required Korean translation affects national-phase status and possible withdrawal; treatment differs based on filing date (see separate entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of translation submission varies by filing date (pre-2015 vs post-2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application was filed before Dec 31, 2014, translations of description, claims, drawings and abstract submitted as of the filing date are considered as the specification/drawings under Article 42(2). Where filed after Jan 1, 2015, the description, claims and drawings submitted as of the filing date are considered to be the specification and drawings as originally filed pursuant to Article 42(2); abstract translation rules differ by language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different transitional rules apply depending on the international filing date; examiners should follow date-based rules when assessing original filing content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner attention to national-phase PCT details and priority treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: When an international application enters the national phase with Korean translation submitted and claims priority under the PCT, the priority claim is treated as the priority claim under the Treaty. If the application serving as the priority basis is Korean or an international application where Korea is the only designated State, the priority claim is considered domestic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an international application serves as the basis of domestic priority and becomes 'another application' under Article 29(3), the application is considered laid open at international publication time, but the scope of inventions is limited to those described in the specification/claims/drawings as of the international filing date and as in the domestic priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure-exception submissions for international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For an international application, a person intending to claim disclosure exceptions pursuant to Article 30(1) may submit a written statement and evidential documents within 30 days from the reference date (period designated for document submission in Korea, or the examination request date if filed within that period), even if such purport was not stated in the written international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a limited opportunity to add disclosure-exception purport/documentation after international filing for national phase considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority where prior-filed app is international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a prior-filed application that serves as a basis for domestic priority is an international application, inventions commonly stated in both the application with domestic priority claim and the international application (limited to specification/claims/drawings submitted at the international filing date) are considered filed at the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider the international filing date as the effective date for commonly stated inventions in domestic priority analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Korean translation of PCT Article 19/34 amendments considered voluntary amendment if timely
rubrics_metrics.description: If Korean translation of written amendments regarding description or claims under PCT Articles 19 and 34 is submitted within the reference date, the examiner proceeds considering the international application to have been voluntarily amended according to Article 47 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely translation of PCT amendments affects the scope of what is treated as filed/ amended in national phase examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may request ISR/IPER-cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may request the applicant of an international application to submit copies of documents cited in the International Search Report or International Preliminary Examination Report; if necessary, the Commissioner of KIPO may request the submission within the designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests may be made in the examiner's name or under the Commissioner's authority, and applicants should comply within designated periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provisions for enlarged concept of novelty for international applications (date-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: A special provision with respect to an enlarged concept of novelty applies depending on filing dates of the international application and of the 'another application' referenced in Article 29(3). Rules differ for cases where filings occurred before Dec 31, 2014 (or where one was before that date) and where filings occurred after Jan 1, 2015, particularly regarding whether the scope of inventions of an international 'another application' is limited to the inventions described as of international filing date and its translation or as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an international application is deemed withdrawn for failure to file a Korean translation per Article 201(4), it cannot be considered 'another application' for application of the enlarged concept of novelty. Examiners must apply the date-specific rules when assessing novelty across international/domestic filings.
